method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE (a trial in a State or Territory court, and comment on silence at a summary trial, answer `not covered`, asserted); every court finding or discretion asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Evidence Act 1995, the compilation registered as C2025C00340 (Compilation No. 35, compilation date 2025-06-10; Federal Register of Legislation, retrieved 2026-10-13), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A04858.txt. No instrument brought in.

checks.command: l4 run ea95-accused.l4 ; l4 run ea95-cases-accused.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the accused's seat: s 4 with the Dictionary's 'federal court' and 'criminal proceeding'; ss 12, 13, 17, 18, 20; ss 59, 60, 65, 66, 67; ss 81-86, 89, 90; ss 94, 97, 98, 100, 101; ss 110, 112; ss 118, 119, 122, 123 (ss 121, 124-126 as one fact); s 128(1)-(10); ss 135, 137, 138, 139; s 141. Out: the rest of Chapter 2, Part 3.3, ss 87, 88, Part 3.5, Part 3.7, s 111, Part 3.9, s 120, ss 126A-127, s 128A, public interest immunity, ss 136, 140, 142 onwards, Chapter 5, civil proceedings. A case in a State or Territory court answers `not covered` (Judiciary Act 1903 s 79 picks up that State's or Territory's evidence law).
seat: the accused person (the defendant in a criminal proceeding)
